To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

“VCL’s visual formalism is modular and can express structural properties of a system and their constraints in a visual and rigorous manner, and can be used as a visual language to express requirements”.
VCL is a formal, visual, modular and extensible language for the specification of structural properties and constraints.

VCL’s approach is to use a visual language to express formally what is not visually expressed by other visual languages; and that VCL’s approach can be used to specify the structural properties and their constraints of software systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of visual languages and tools for specifying structural properties and their constraints formally, visually and modularly.
the formalisation of visual languages, in particular, with the formalisation, visualisation and modularisation of structural modelling.
the development of VCL, which is an attempt to provide a visual, formal and rigorous language for the specification of software systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

VCL is a new language for the visual specification of structural properties and constraints of software systems, that provides a visual and formal way to describe structural properties, and to specify constraints on structural properties, in a modular way, and that is supported by a visual editor, VCL-Editor.
VCL provides a visual language with a formal semantics for the structural modelling of software systems.
the VCL language is a promising approach to the specification of structural properties of software systems and their constraints.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VCL is a formal language that allows the specification of structural properties and their constraints visually, formally and modularly.
VCL provides a visual language with the rigour of a formal one, and with a modular design that supports the separation of concerns in software specification.
VCL provides a visual, formal and rigorous language for specifying structural properties and their constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of VCL for structural modelling can be seen as a step in the direction of a more general approach to visual modelling based on a visual language that can be used to specify the semantics of any visual language.
the visual representation of structural properties is a valuable tool for requirements engineering.
the use of a formal visual language can be a valuable tool to help the designer to specify the structure of a system in an abstract way.
